newsitem.title: UK: UK bill to fight millennium computer bug moves on.
newsitem.headline: UK bill to fight millennium computer bug moves on.

text.p: A bill aimed at averting the risk of computers being unable to cope with the dawn of the new millennium cleared an important parliamentary hurdle on Friday.

Conservative member of parliament David Atkinson's bill would require British companies to conduct an audit of the capacity of their computer systems to deal with calendar dates after December 31, 1999.
Industry experts have warned of possible "Millennium Bug" chaos because the year in most computer programmes is expressed as a double digit -- currently 97.
The risk is that, unless properly programmed, computers will be flummoxed by a double-zero for 2000 and will go haywire.

The bill, which was given an unopposed second reading in the lower House of Commons, would also require company directors to report to shareholders on steps they are taking to ensure essential computers are being programmed to tackle the problem.

The bill, which takes the form of an amendment to the Companies Act 1985, has a good chance of becoming law if time can be found in the tight parliamentary tiemtable for it to clear its remaining stages.
